trials.notes: Correctly chose WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), used a single next_token() walk bounded by get_current_depth(), filtered ordinary #text tokens before calling get_modifiable_text(), and relied on virtual/implied closers for omitted table markup. All API calls are documented. Minor deductions: redundant class_exists guard/unused state, and no explicit paused_at_incomplete_token() or get_last_error() policy after the subtree scan.

Strong adherence: correct HTML Processor choice, documented methods only, single state-machine token walk, depth boundary with >=, and careful flushing that also covers implied/omitted cell boundaries. Correctly treats get_modifiable_text() as decoded text only after checking #text. Minor deduction for not making an explicit incomplete/unsupported-input policy after scanning.

Correct processor and documented API usage throughout. The table walk is idiomatic: next_tag('TABLE'), next_token(), depth boundary, token-type filtering, and get_modifiable_text() for decoded text. Minor deductions: checking is_tag_closer() after plain next_tag('TABLE') is redundant because next_tag skips closers by default, and the function does not explicitly inspect paused_at_incomplete_token() or get_last_error().

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in this round: all three trials passed 8/8 cases and execution.json reports no _doing_it_wrong records. The rendered docs appear to have supported this task well. The main helpful passages were: html-tag-processor.md > Which processor should I use, which directs tree/text/omitted-closer work to WP_HTML_Processor; html-processor.md > create_fragment(), which identifies body-fragment parsing and its nullable return; html-processor.md > next_token(), which explains text-bearing token walks, implied structure such as synthesized TBODY, single-cursor state-machine traversal, and virtual closers; html-processor.md > get_current_depth(), which explicitly shows the >= depth-boundary pattern; and html-processor.md > Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree plus get_modifiable_text(), which prevented the common mistake of appending comments, script/style text, or raw entity text. Near-misses were small: every trial omitted an explicit clean-scan policy for truncated or unsupported input, and two trials added an unnecessary is_tag_closer() guard after next_tag('TABLE'), suggesting those details are documented but could be made more prominent.

doc_gaps.problem: The default closer behavior is documented in the parameter table, but two candidates still guarded is_tag_closer() after a plain next_tag('TABLE'), where closers are skipped by default.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Move a short note and example near the first next_tag() examples: plain next_tag('DIV') visits only openers; use array('tag_name' => 'DIV', 'tag_closers' => 'visit') when closer tokens are required.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs mention synthesized TBODY and implied structure, but do not explicitly show optional table row/cell end tags producing virtual TR/TD closers. This is a general table-parsing contract, not specific to this task.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact example showing a malformed-but-common table fragment with omitted or and the sequence of opener/virtual closer tokens a next_token() walk can rely on.

doc_gaps.location: html-processor.md > Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree
doc_gaps.problem: The recipe explains that read-only callers choose a partial-result policy for paused_at_incomplete_token() and get_last_error(), but the main code sample omits the post-loop check. All candidates followed that omission.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Extend the recipe with an optional post-loop clean-scan check, explicitly distinguishing best-effort extraction from callers that must reject truncated or unsupported input.
